claims.head: A shadow job for Howden, Karlsson and Holtz
claims.call: The Golden Knights’ L2 (Howden, Karlsson and Holtz) spends at least 52% of its 5-on-5 time against the Senators’ first line.
claims.body: At home, the Golden Knights keep sending Karlsson’s line (Howden, Karlsson and Holtz) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Ryan Craig has been giving this group the hard job of facing the other team’s top line. Tonight the Senators’ first line is Zetterlund, Stützle and Giroux.

claims.gist: At home, Ryan Craig likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Senators’ first line.

notes.text: The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 23% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the second-lowest in the league (a typical team: 43%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
Thomas Chabot is out 1-2 weeks (upper body injury) and has missed the last 2 games. He is a top-pair defenseman. Tyler Kleven has taken his spot beside Jordan Spence.
William Eklund is out 10-12 weeks and has missed the last 7 games.
Artem Zub was added to the roster on Oct 16 and has played beside Jake Sanderson.
Jordan Spence has started killing penalties: on the ice for 33% of the team’s shorthanded time in 11 games, up from 4% last season.
Mitch Marner is away for personal reasons and missed their last game. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Alexander Holtz has taken his spot beside William Karlsson and Brett Howden.
Alexander Holtz was added to the roster on Oct 23 and has played beside William Karlsson and Brett Howden.

VGK.head: The Golden Knights have a slight edge
VGK.body: Even though Vegas will be without Marner, the Golden Knights have been out-chancing opponents lately and have home-ice advantage. Still, it’s close: the Senators can make it interesting if they keep dangerous shots away.
